subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.j@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum. TL;DR: PulseMed is a strong fit for Redwood Dedicated to meet your latency, throughput, and HIPAA/isolation needs; next steps are a technical deep-dive with Monica, a draft SOW/pricing for reserved capacity, and procurement contact for contracting.

1) Pain points you described:
- Latency spikes during peak 9–11am ET affecting clinical UI response (P95 observed ~320–450ms, occasional P99 >750ms)
- Need for guaranteed isolation and controls for PHI (VPC, KMS, audit logs)
- Predictable unit economics: want committed monthly capacity to reduce per-token cost and avoid throttling during batch jobs for overnight inference

2) Goals
- Provide 24/7 production capacity with 99.9% uptime SLA and predictable latency targets for interactive workflows (target P95 <350ms for production routes)
- Support batch inference jobs (overnight) without impacting interactive latency
- Enterprise controls: SOC 2, encryption at rest, audit logs, and dedicated customer networking

3) Proposed Dedicated configuration (starter proposal)
- Reserved pool: 8x A100 (or equivalent) GPUs pinned to PulseMed account with customer-isolated tenancy
- Autoscale / burst: allow bursting up to 12 GPUs for scheduled batch windows (policy-based)
- Replication/HA: 2 GPU redundancy (one hot spare) to meet SLA targets
- Routing: latency-first routing for interactive endpoints; batch endpoints routed to lower-priority nodes with pre-warm windows
- Expected baseline performance (estimate): at 80 concurrent req/s, ~150 tokens per request, we expect P95 <350ms with continuous batching and prefix caching enabled

4) Billing & commercial items
- Committed monthly fee for reserved pool + usage for burst hours and storage. I’ll send a draft SOW and pricing sheet after we confirm sizing and SLAs.

5) Next steps
- Technical deep-dive with Monica (Solutions Engineer) — 60m to validate exact model variants, batching strategy, and network setup
- Procurement contact / PO path from PulseMed to begin drafting contract and pricing
- Share SOC2 / compliance artifacts (attached)

I attached a short capacity plan (PulseMed_dedicated_capacity_plan_20270428.pdf) and our SOC2 attestation for review. Please let me know availability for a technical deep-dive — Monica and Marissa are available next Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Ben — thanks for the thorough recap and for sending the artifacts. This matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Encryption/KMS: we need keys managed in our AWS KMS (customer-managed keys) and full disk encryption for any attached storage. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS and provide key-rotation logs?
- Data residency: production traffic will be US-only; please confirm region alignment and that logs/audit trails won’t transit outside region boundaries.
- SLA: 99.9% is acceptable as a baseline — can we include a P99 latency objective (not a hard SLA) as a target for interactive endpoints?
- Procurement: procurement@pulsemed.com is the right inbox for contracting (cc’d). For pricing — we’re evaluating committed+burst model; please include an estimate for committed-only (8 GPUs) and a second line item for burst usage to 12 GPUs/month.

We’re available for the technical deep-dive on Wed 2027-05-05 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 2027-05-06 09:00–10:00 PT. Monica and Marissa being on that call will be great.

Appreciate it — Alex

Following up with a few technical notes ahead of the deep-dive so Alex and the PulseMed team can review: 

- KMS: Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS integration for private deployments. We can configure envelope encryption where the data key is wrapped by your KMS CMK; audit logs for key usage are available. Will confirm exact key rotation windows during the call.
- Network & residency: we’ll deploy the tenant in the selected us-east-1 region and VPC peering/VPN options will keep traffic within your network boundaries. We collect audit logs (immutable) and can configure retention per your policy.
- Caching / batching: recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for your most common prompts (clinical note completion) to reduce tokens and improve P95. For batch jobs, we’ll use an isolated routing policy and schedule pre-warm to avoid cold-start latency.
- Model variants & fallback: propose primary: redwood-v2-clinical-13B (quantized) with a fallback to redwood-v2-clinical-7B for heavy load periods; both tested for quality in our eval harness.
- HA and capacity: 8x A100 gives you ~2x headroom for interactive traffic with our batching assumptions; burst to 12x covers scheduled overnight batch spikes. We’ll include a simulated perf run in the SOW (24h load test) before final commit.
- Estimate: rough engineering estimate for committed + baseline usage (8 GPUs) = $X/month (will include numbers in commercial doc).

I’ll prepare a short appendix with the technical config we’d use and attach it to the SOW. Looking forward to the deep-dive — Wed 2027-05-05 10:00 PT works for me.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
